newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Power, STT to take foreign telecoms partner.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Power, STT to take foreign telecoms partner.

text.p: Singapore Power and Singapore Technologies Telemedia (STT) will bid for a licence to operate fixed-line telephone services in Singapore with a foreign company or consortium, Singapore Power said on Wednesday.

A Singapore Power spokeswoman told Reuters a decision had not yet been taken on which foreign partner or partners to team up with for the right to compete with the current telephone monopoly, Singapore Telecom, (SingTel).
"We are actively discussing with foreign telecommunications companies. Many have approached us and we are having discussions as to who it will be," the spokeswoman said in a telephone interview.
"The decision has not been made and the composition of the joint venture parties will be announced in due course when discussions are finished," she added.
The Singapore government said in September it would allow one or two new operators to compete with SingTel when the market is deregulated in April 2000.
Foreign companies have been encouraged to join local firms to bid for the licence. Foreign companies can own up to 49 percent of any bidding consortium.
Singapore Power, the island's electricity and gas utlity, and STT are both owned by state investment company Temasek Holdings.
Analysts say they have an extremely good chance of getting one of the new licences since they could use their existing infrastructure as the basis for a telecoms network.

Singapore Power's president and chief executive Boey Tak Hap was quoted by the Straits Times on Wednesday as saying use of the company's underground cable network for telecommunications "would add value and augment returns to shareholders".

"We have the ability to quickly roll out all these new services such as video-on-demand and other interactive information, and in doing so will be making better use of our assets," the daily newspaper quoted Boey as saying.

British Telecom Plc (BT) and its U.S. merger partner MCI Communications Corp, as well as AT&T of the United States and the Global One alliance of Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom AG are all reported to be considering bidding for a Singapore licence.
Cable and Wireless's majority-owned unit Hong Kong Telecom has also expressed an interest in a licence.
The Singapore Power spokeswoman declined to comment when asked if BT was their most likely foreign partner: "We are looking at a foreign partner or a foreign consortium."
Singapore Power has said a successful bid for the licence could involve up to S$1 billion in infrastructure investment.
Up to six telecommunications consortiums are expected to bid for the licence.

In addition to the Singapore Power/STT bid, Britain's Cable & Wireless, and a partnership of Singapore Press Holdings (SPH) and Keppel Telecommunications and Transportation Ltd (KTT) have both said they will bid.
